title: Densest packings of two translates of a lattice in five dimensions: paper, certificate, verification programs and Lean 4 formalization
description:
Let Λ be a lattice in R^5 and b a vector outside Λ such that distinct points of Λ ∪ (Λ + b) are at distance at least 2. The paper proves that the covolume of Λ is at least 16√2, so no packing of unit balls centred at two translates of a lattice in R^5 is denser than the D5 lattice packing, and that equality holds for exactly five configurations up to congruence: three splittings of √2 D5 into two cosets of a sublattice of index two, the uniform packing with kissing configuration Q5, and Leech's 2-periodic layered packing with kissing configuration L5. Every Voronoi cell of such a set has volume at least 8√2.

The proof reduces the bound to the vertices and edges of a locally finite polyhedron in the space of symmetric 6 × 6 matrices; up to symmetry it has 34 vertices, whose cones have 80,695 extreme rays in 480 orbits. cert/certificate.txt records this computation in exact arithmetic. checkers/ holds four independent checkers of the certificate (C, C++, Julia, Python) and two double-description enumerations of the extreme rays (C, Julia); cddlib and lrs recompute the rays as well. lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project whose theorem D5.certificate proves in the kernel every vertex and edge statement of the certificate, without native_decide, using only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The equality case is proved by hand in the paper. run_all.sh runs every check; dist/ holds the PDF, the LaTeX source zip, the arXiv tarball and MasterD5TwoTranslatesZip.zip with every file of the repository.
